<a id="page-export"></a>

## About this page

Writes the whole vault to a file: either still encrypted, or in plain text for another app to read.

#### How it works

**Stays encrypted** keeps every password protected. [Plain text](/guide/settings/export/#group-export-plain) writes them out for anyone to read, and asks first.

Apart from the WM Pass vault, which is a copy of the whole file, every export leaves out the trash. Attachments are kept in their own files beside the vault, and no export includes them.

#### When to use it

To move to another app, to keep a copy you can open without WM Pass, or to print a paper copy to lock away. For regular copies you can restore, use [Backups](/guide/settings/backup/).

#### Limits

Exporting does not ask for your master password. Anyone at your unlocked vault could export it, which is one more reason to keep [Lock after no activity](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-after) short.

See also [Moving passwords in and out](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-import-export), [Import](/guide/settings/import/), [Backups](/guide/settings/backup/), [Lock after no activity](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-after).

<a id="action-export-wmvault"></a>

## WM Pass vault

Saves a copy of the vault file itself, still encrypted. It opens in WM Pass with the same passwords, key files and security keys as this vault.

#### How it works

Any changes still waiting to be saved are written first, so the copy is up to date.

#### Limits

Attachments are not in it, since they live in their own files beside the vault. The trash and the hidden shelf are, as they are part of the file.

The copy keeps every way in this vault has now, duress passwords included. Changing your password later does not change the copy.

See also [Backups](/guide/settings/backup/), [The vault file](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-vault-file), [Change it and rekey](/guide/settings/security/#action-rekey).

<a id="action-export-kdbx"></a>

## KeePass database

Writes a new KeePass database (KDBX 4) protected by a password you choose. KeePass, KeePassXC and other apps that read KDBX can open it.

#### How it works

The database uses Argon2id to protect its password. Before it is saved, WM Pass reads it back and checks that every login came through intact.

Items of other kinds keep their fields, with a WM Pass kind field saying what they were.

#### Limits

Items on the hidden shelf are left out.

Folders are not kept: every item goes into one group. Each login keeps one web address, and attachments and passkeys are not included.

Anyone with the file can try passwords against it for as long as they like, so give it a long one.

See also [Import](/guide/settings/import/), [Hidden shelf](/guide/settings/shelf/).

<a id="group-export-plain"></a>

## Plain text

These exports write out every password, note and one-time code secret as readable text. Anyone who gets the file can read all of it.

#### How it works

WM Pass asks before writing one, and saves it where you choose. Items on the hidden shelf are included.

#### Limits

Keep the file off shared drives, and out of folders that sync to the cloud, where old versions can be kept.

Delete it as soon as you are done, and empty the recycle bin. A deleted file can stay readable on the disk for a while.

See also [Bitwarden JSON](/guide/settings/export/#action-export-bitwarden), [CSV](/guide/settings/export/#action-export-csv), [Printable page](/guide/settings/export/#action-export-html), [PDF or printer](/guide/settings/export/#action-export-pdf), [Hidden shelf](/guide/settings/shelf/).

<a id="action-export-bitwarden"></a>

## Bitwarden JSON

Writes Bitwarden's unencrypted JSON, which Bitwarden and many other password managers can import.

#### How it works

Kinds Bitwarden does not have become secure notes, with their values as custom fields.

#### Limits

It is [plain text](/guide/settings/export/#group-export-plain): anyone who opens the file can read every password.

See also [Plain text](/guide/settings/export/#group-export-plain).

<a id="action-export-csv"></a>

## CSV

Writes a spreadsheet file with one row per item, in WM Pass's own columns. WM Pass can import it back.

#### How it works

The columns are kind, folder, title, username, password, web addresses, one-time code, notes, tags and other fields. Custom fields, and the fields of kinds other than logins, go in the last column.

#### Limits

It is [plain text](/guide/settings/export/#group-export-plain): anyone who opens the file can read every password.

See also [Plain text](/guide/settings/export/#group-export-plain), [Import](/guide/settings/import/).

<a id="action-export-html"></a>

## Printable page

Writes a web page listing every item and its values, made to be printed and locked away.

#### How it works

Open it in a browser and print it. The page carries a warning at the top that anyone holding it can read everything on it.

#### Limits

One-time codes appear as their setup links, which hold the secret.

The file is [plain text](/guide/settings/export/#group-export-plain) until you delete it, and the paper can be read by anyone who finds it.

See also [Plain text](/guide/settings/export/#group-export-plain), [Emergency kit](/guide/settings/security/#action-emergency-kit).

<a id="action-export-pdf"></a>

## PDF or printer

*Only in Android.*

Hands the printable page to Android's print screen, which saves it as a PDF or sends it to a printer.

#### How it works

Choose **Save as PDF** there and pick where the file goes, or choose a printer. The page carries a warning at the top that anyone holding it can read everything on it.

#### Limits

One-time codes appear as their setup links, which hold the secret.

Like the other [plain-text](/guide/settings/export/#group-export-plain) exports, the PDF is not encrypted: anyone who opens it can read everything until you delete it, and the paper can be read by anyone who finds it.

See also [Plain text](/guide/settings/export/#group-export-plain), [Printable page](/guide/settings/export/#action-export-html).
